concept_name: Conservative vs Non-Conservative Forces — the Round-Trip Test
source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.6 Work, Energy and Power — table-of-contents scope only (conservative and non-conservative forces sit between the work definitions and potential energy), teaching authored from first principles. The atomic concept: a force is CONSERVATIVE when the total work it does around any closed path is exactly zero — equivalently, its work depends only on the endpoints, never on the path taken. Gravity is the conservative exemplar: its along-track pull never changes direction, so the outbound leg's negative work is exactly cancelled by the return leg's positive work. Friction is NOT conservative: because it always points against the instantaneous motion, its work is negative on the way out AND on the way back, so a round trip ADDS the two losses instead of cancelling them. Does NOT define potential energy (potential_energy_definition, #6, which builds directly on the endpoint property proved here), does NOT do energy conservation (#9), does NOT account for where friction's negative work goes (#10), and does NOT re-teach the work definition (work_done_by_constant_force, #1), the sign taxonomy (positive_negative_zero_work, #2) or kinetic energy (kinetic_energy_definition, #3) — all prerequisites, consumed and never re-derived. The spring is deliberately absent: it cannot be represented in a per-step work ledger, so 'the spring is also conservative' is ceded to elastic_potential_energy_spring (#8). Built on the newtons_laws_body field_3d engine with the SEAM K/L/M/N energy layer (docs/loop_runs/ch6_state.md) — the first concept in the fleet to exercise the round-trip start-line latch (checkpoints seeded exactly at the home pose, capture_mode 'every') alongside the 'every' pass-1/pass-2 interior stamps, and the first to author the SEAM-M teaching DWELL: every checkpoint is a labelled point (marker 'point') and the scene's physics HOLDS for 1.5-2.5 s on a stamped crossing so a teacher can read the values before the motion resumes.

real_world_anchor.primary: A heavy bag lifted onto a shelf and later brought back down. While the bag goes up, gravity's work on it is negative; while it comes down, gravity's work is positive and equal in size — over the up-and-down round trip, gravity's total work is exactly zero.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Sliding a box across the floor to a door and dragging it back. Friction points against the box on the way out and against it again on the way back: its work is negative on both legs, and the round trip adds the two losses instead of cancelling them.

s.name: position along the track
s.derived: the integrator's own live value; no slider anywhere in this concept writes s directly

W_gravity.name: work done by gravity, running ledger

W_friction.name: work done by friction, running ledger
W_friction.derived: engine-integrated per step as -f * abs(ds), never a closed form in s alone because it depends on total PATH traveled, not net displacement

constraints: gravity's work over any closed path on this incline sums to exactly zero: W_gravity_round_trip = 0, because W_gravity depends only on (s - s0), never on the path taken to get there
friction's work is never positive while the block is sliding: W_friction_leg <= 0 on every leg, because kinetic friction always opposes the instantaneous velocity
friction's round-trip work is strictly more negative than either leg alone: W_friction_round_trip = -2*mu_k*m*g*cos(theta)*d_up, never zero and never positive for any real trip
the round trip can only happen if tan(theta) > mu_s (this concept's guided states: tan25 = 0.466 > mu 0.3, margin 1.55x); otherwise the block sticks at the top and never returns

every guided launch stays strictly inside the +/-6 m track: the highest apex is S4's at s = +5.12 m (v0 = 8.5 m/s frictionless from s0 = -3.6 m) and the lowest reset point is S3's at s = -5.27 m, so no state ever reaches a geometric bound and the clamp artifact is unreachable by construction

N = m*g*cos(theta) > 0 at every authored theta in this concept (5 deg to 45 deg on S5's slider, fixed 25 deg on S1-S4); no applied force anywhere, so N never clamps to zero and lift-off is never reachable
g = 9.8 m/s^2 (engine constant NLB_G); m = 5 kg fixed in every one of the five states, never a slider anywhere in this concept

aha_moment.statement: The same round trip that erases gravity's work makes friction's work larger, not zero.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: Two work bars and point A: the block halts there for 2.5 s on the return while gravity reads 0.0 J and friction reads minus 125.3 J on the same held line.

STATE_1.title: Gravity's total work over a round trip is zero

scene_composition.text: a 5 kg block launched up a frictionless 25° slope at 8 m/s from its home pose at s = −3.6 m; it climbs 7.73 m over 1.93 s, turns at the apex (s = +4.13 m) and slides back down, a 3.86 s round trip
the inclined slope, θ = 25°, frictionless, track length 6 m
the weight arrow mg, its mg·sinθ and mg·cosθ components shown, holding the same direction through the whole loop
the gravity work bar: falls to −160.0 J at the apex, climbs back through zero, and swings briefly green (up to +41.6 J) after the block runs on past its start line
the d arrow grows to 7.726 m, shrinks, and vanishes as the block re-crosses its start line, then re-grows briefly down-slope

point A, a track-level dot seeded exactly at the home pose (marker 'point', capture_mode 'every'): it stamps 0.0 J at the departure and RE-stamps on the return as 'point A (pass 2): W gravity = 0.0 J'. dwell_from_pass 2 skips the departure and freezes the whole scene for 2500 ms on the RETURN crossing (T = 3863 → 6363 ms), badge 'paused: point A'. 'every' is required, not cosmetic — a home-pose checkpoint fires at t = 0, so under 'first' the stamp would freeze on the departure reading and never show the return crossing this state exists to prove

tts_sentences.text_en: The block leaves point A up a frictionless slope at eight metres per second.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Block point A से आठ metres per second की speed से एक frictionless slope पर ऊपर जाता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Gravity's meter falls as it climbs, then climbs back as it slides down again.
tts_sentences.text_hi: जैसे-जैसे block ऊपर चढ़ता है, gravity का meter गिरता है, फिर जब block नीचे slide करता है तो meter वापस चढ़ता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Back at point A the motion pauses: total work by gravity, zero joules.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Point A पर वापस आते ही motion रुक जाता है: gravity द्वारा किया गया total work, zero joules।

tts_sentences.text_en: Up and back to the same place, gravity's total work returns to zero.
tts_sentences.text_hi: ऊपर जाकर उसी जगह वापस आने पर, gravity का total work zero पर लौट आता है।

STATE_2.title: Friction: a round trip does not cancel its work

scene_composition.text: the same 5 kg block, same launch (8 m/s), but the slope is now rough (μₛ = μₖ = 0.3) — it climbs only 4.70 m against STATE_1's 7.73 m, a 3.70 s round trip
the inclined slope, θ = 25°, μ = 0.3, track length 6 m — no friction arrow drawn yet (it debuts in STATE_3)
the weight arrow mg, unchanged direction throughout
the gravity work bar repeats STATE_1's fall-and-return shape exactly (position-only)
the friction work bar falls to −62.6 J at the apex and KEEPS falling on the way down — never climbs

two track-level points 2.0 m apart, both 'every'. Point B at +2.0 m stamps 'point B: W gravity = −41.4 J · W friction = −26.6 J' outbound (T = 284) and '(pass 2) … W friction = −98.6 J' on the return (T = 4588), holding the scene 1500 ms each time — gravity repeats, friction has grown, and the pause is what lets a teacher compare them. Point A at the home pose stamps 0.0 J for both ledgers at the departure and re-stamps on the return as 'point A (pass 2): W gravity = 0.0 J · W friction = −125.3 J', holding 2500 ms (T = 6698 → 9198) — that held line IS the concept's PRIMARY aha, and under 'first' it would read a frozen 0.0 J for friction, asserting the exact misconception this state destroys

tts_sentences.text_en: The slope is rough now, same launch from point A.
tts_sentences.text_hi: अब slope rough है, point A से वही launch।

tts_sentences.text_en: At point B the meters pause going up, then again coming down.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Point B पर meters ऊपर जाते समय रुकते हैं, फिर नीचे आते समय दोबारा।

tts_sentences.text_en: Back at point A: gravity zero, friction minus one hundred twenty-five point three joules.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Point A पर वापस: gravity zero, friction minus one hundred twenty-five point three joules।

tts_sentences.text_en: Friction is negative both ways, so the trip adds the losses: gravity is conservative, friction is not.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Friction दोनों तरफ negative है, इसलिए trip दोनों losses को जोड़ देती है: gravity conservative है, friction नहीं।

misconception_watch.belief: Retracing the path reverses friction's work the way it reverses gravity's
misconception_watch.visual_counter: At point B, gravity stamps −41.4 J on both passes while friction's stamp falls from −26.6 J to −98.6 J — the scene halts 1.5 s on each pass so the two can be read against each other; point A then halts 2.5 s reading 'W gravity = 0.0 J, W friction = −125.3 J'.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Friction's work is negative on every leg, so a round trip adds the two losses — it never cancels them.

scene_composition.text: the same block, a slower launch (7 m/s) on the same rough slope (μ = 0.3) — a 3.24 s round trip climbing 3.60 m, with both point-A passes held long enough to read
the inclined slope, θ = 25°, μ = 0.3, track length 6 m
the weight arrow mg — never changes direction through the whole loop, the counter-evidence for the misconception
the friction arrow, debuting in this state: points down-slope while the block climbs, then FLIPS 180° to point up-slope at the turnaround (t = 1029 ms) and stays flipped through the descent
the friction work bar keeps falling through the reversal instead of climbing back — the flip does not undo the loss, it IS the loss's cause

point A, a track-level dot at +1.5 m, stamps 'point A: W friction = −20.0 J' outbound and '(pass 2) −75.9 J' on the return, freezing the scene 2000 ms each time (T = 243 → 2243 and T = 4715 → 6715) — same place, motion reversed, the loss 3.8× larger, and each number standing still long enough to be read

tts_sentences.text_en: The friction arrow points down the slope on the way up.
tts_sentences.text_hi: ऊपर जाते समय friction का arrow slope की नीचे की दिशा में point करता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: At the top it flips to point up the slope instead.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Top पर पहुँचते ही यह flip होकर slope की ऊपर की दिशा में point करने लगता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Friction always opposes the motion; the weight arrow never turns.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Friction हमेशा motion के विपरीत होता है; weight का arrow कभी नहीं मुड़ता।

tts_sentences.text_en: At point A the motion pauses twice: minus twenty joules, then minus seventy-five point nine — the loss grows.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Point A पर motion दो बार रुकता है: पहले minus twenty joules, फिर minus seventy-five point nine -- loss बढ़ता जाता है।

misconception_watch.belief: A force keeps its direction; the return leg just runs it in reverse
misconception_watch.visual_counter: At the turnaround the friction arrow swings 180 degrees to point up-slope while the weight arrow holds its direction; the friction bar keeps falling through the reversal instead of climbing back.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Friction turns around with the block, so it pushes against the motion on the way down as well — its work is negative on both legs.

STATE_4.title: Gravity's work depends only on position

scene_composition.text: the same block, a faster frictionless launch (8.5 m/s) — a longer, higher flight than STATE_1's (climb 8.72 m vs 7.73 m) over a 4.11 s round trip
the inclined slope, θ = 25°, frictionless, track length 6 m
the weight arrow mg, holding its direction throughout
the gravity work bar climbs to −180.6 J near the top; no ledger stays at zero here, it is the two points below that carry the claim
point A, a track-level dot at +3.0 m, stamps 'point A: W gravity = −62.1 J' outbound (no dwell) and '(pass 2) −62.1 J' — identical — on the return, where the scene holds 2000 ms (T = 5715 → 7715)

point B, a track-level dot at +6.0 m, stamps 'point B: W gravity = −124.2 J' outbound and '(pass 2) −124.2 J' — identical — on the return, holding 2000 ms (T = 3199 → 5199); the two points are 3.0 m apart, so their captions can never overlap

tts_sentences.text_en: Launched faster, the block flies higher, still frictionless.
tts_sentences.text_hi: तेज़ speed से launch होने पर, block ऊँचा उड़ता है, फिर भी frictionless।

tts_sentences.text_en: Point A reads minus sixty-two point one; point B, minus one hundred twenty-four point two.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Point A minus sixty-two point one पढ़ता है; point B, minus one hundred twenty-four point two।

tts_sentences.text_en: Coming back, the motion pauses at each: both readings repeat exactly.
tts_sentences.text_hi: वापस आते समय, motion हर एक पर रुकता है: दोनों readings बिल्कुल वैसी ही दोहराई जाती हैं।

tts_sentences.text_en: Gravity's work depends only on start and end points, so each point gets one number—potential energy, the next concept.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Gravity का work सिर्फ start और end points पर निर्भर करता है, इसलिए हर point को एक number मिलता है -- potential energy, अगला concept।

scene_composition.text: the block opens MOVING — v₀ = 8 m/s up the μ = 0.3 slope (the STATE_2 trip) — then continues to the track end and wraps, re-zeroing both ledgers and the d arrow in the same frame
the inclined slope, θ live on the slider (default 25°), μₛ and μₖ live (default 0.3)
both the weight arrow and the friction arrow are live — friction flips with every turnaround, weight never changes
both work bars run live on a 220 J scale — set friction to zero and gravity's total always returns to zero every lap; raise friction and it keeps falling every leg
the d arrow tracks the block's live displacement from its current home pose, re-anchoring at each wrap
four live dials: incline angle θ (5°–45°), static friction μₛ, kinetic friction μₖ (both 0–0.6), and launch speed v₀ (0–9 m/s)

tts_sentences.text_en: Change the slope, the friction, and the launch speed.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Slope, friction, और launch speed बदलिए।

tts_sentences.text_en: Turn friction to zero and gravity's total always returns to zero.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Friction को zero कर दीजिए और gravity का total हमेशा zero पर लौट आएगा।

tts_sentences.text_en: Raise friction high enough and the block stops partway — it never gets back.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Friction को काफी ज़्यादा बढ़ा दीजिए और block बीच में ही रुक जाएगा -- यह कभी वापस नहीं पहुँचता।

regeneration_variants.label: A Suitcase Sent Up and Down a Boarding Ramp
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A suitcase is launched up a boarding ramp, turns, and slides back down. On a smooth ramp it returns exactly to its start; on a rough one, dragging against the ramp both ways, it does not.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical readings: the same round-trip gravity ledger returning to 0.0 J on the smooth ramp, and the same friction ledger falling on both legs on the rough one, latching a larger negative total on the return.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same single-body incline rig — only the labelled object changes from a block to a suitcase.

regeneration_variants.label: A Delivery Cart Pushed Up and Down a Loading Ramp
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A delivery cart is given a push up a loading ramp, turns at the top, and rolls back down. A dry ramp lets it return to its start; a wet, rough ramp costs it a little more with every metre in either direction.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Same closed-path test: gravity's total work over the round trip is zero regardless of ramp condition, while friction's total is always negative and always larger in size than either single leg.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same rig and physics — the block is relabelled a cart, the slope is the loading ramp.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student who has mastered this concept can state that a force is conservative when its total work around any closed path is zero, equivalently when its work depends only on the endpoints; can explain that friction is non-conservative because its work is negative on every leg of a trip, so a round trip adds the losses instead of cancelling them; can identify that friction's direction reverses with the motion while gravity's does not, and connect that difference to the sign of the work on each leg; and can state that a conservative force's work at a given point is the same number no matter which path was used to reach it.

questions.stem: A 2 kg block slides 3 m up a frictionless 30 degree incline and slides back down to its starting point. What is the total work done by gravity over the whole round trip?

distractor_misconceptions.B: computes only the outbound leg's work and stops, forgetting the return leg cancels it
distractor_misconceptions.C: computes only the return leg as if it were the whole trip
distractor_misconceptions.D: doubles the one-way loss instead of the two legs cancelling — the non-conservative-force error, misapplied to gravity

questions.tested_idea: a closed path gives zero total work for a conservative force
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 3 kg crate slides 2 m up a frictionless 20 degree incline and slides back to its starting point. What is the total work done by gravity over the whole round trip?

questions.stem: The same 2 kg block slides 3 m up a 30 degree incline with mu = 0.5 and slides back to its starting point. What is the total work done by friction over the whole round trip?

distractor_misconceptions.A: the concept's headline misconception — assumes the round trip cancels friction's work the way it cancels gravity's
distractor_misconceptions.B: computes only ONE leg's loss and forgets the second leg
distractor_misconceptions.D: doubles the correct total again by mistake

questions.tested_idea: friction's round-trip work adds two negative legs, never cancels
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 4 kg trunk slides 2.5 m up a 25 degree incline with mu = 0.4 and slides back to its starting point. What is the total work done by friction over the whole round trip?

questions.stem: As a block slides up then back down the same rough incline, which force's direction changes, and what does that do to its work?

options.A: Gravity changes direction; its work becomes positive on the return leg
options.B: Friction changes direction; its work stays negative on both legs

distractor_misconceptions.A: swaps which force flips — attributes the reversal to gravity instead of friction
distractor_misconceptions.C: misses that kinetic friction's direction genuinely reverses with velocity
distractor_misconceptions.D: over-applies the flip to gravity too

questions.tested_idea: friction's direction follows the motion; gravity's does not
questions.parallel_form_stem: A block slides up then back down a rough ramp. Which force reverses direction at the turnaround, and what happens to the sign of its work?

questions.stem: On a frictionless slope, point A sits 3.0 m from the launch point. On the way up, gravity's work reading at point A is -62.1 J. What is the reading at point A when the block passes it again on the way down?

options.D: It cannot be -62.1 J twice, because work already done cannot repeat

distractor_misconceptions.B: assumes the return crossing flips the sign — importing friction's direction-flip rule onto gravity
distractor_misconceptions.C: assumes crossing a point a second time resets its reading to zero
distractor_misconceptions.D: assumes a rendered reading must differ if the direction of travel differs

questions.tested_idea: gravity's work is a function of position alone, so the same place gives the same reading
questions.parallel_form_stem: On a frictionless slope, a marked point sits 0.8 m from the launch point and reads -19.6 J on the way up. What does it read when the block crosses it again on the way down?

questions.stem: A force is classified as conservative if...

options.A: its total work around any closed path is zero
options.B: it always points in the same direction as the motion
options.D: it acts only through direct contact

distractor_misconceptions.B: describes something unrelated to the definition — many conservative forces, including gravity, do negative work on part of a trip
distractor_misconceptions.C: assumes conservative means never negative — gravity's own up-leg work is negative; it is the ROUND-TRIP total that must be zero, not each leg
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses conservative with contact-vs-field, unrelated to the actual test

questions.tested_idea: the closed-path test is the definition of a conservative force
questions.parallel_form_stem: Which of these is the correct test for whether a force is conservative?

questions.stem: On the explore slope (theta = 25 degrees), a teacher sets mu_s well above tan(theta) and gives the block a small nudge up the slope. The block slides a short way and comes to rest partway up. What happens to gravity's work reading after the block stops?

options.A: It returns to zero, because every round trip must end at zero
options.B: It holds at whatever negative value the block reached — the block never returns to complete the round trip
options.C: It becomes positive, because the body is now at rest
options.D: It resets to zero automatically after a few seconds

distractor_misconceptions.A: over-generalizes the round-trip-returns-to-zero result to a case where the round trip never actually completes
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses being at rest with the WORK reading, a different quantity entirely
distractor_misconceptions.D: assumes the display auto-resets on a timer instead of on an actual return crossing

questions.tested_idea: the zero-total result only holds once the round trip actually completes
questions.parallel_form_stem: In the same sandbox, mu_s is set below tan(theta) and the block always slides back to the bottom. What does gravity's work reading do at the moment it re-crosses its start line?
